finding: A long-running encrypted balancer (one NameNodeConnector/KeyManager across iterations) keeps using the DataEncryptionKey it cached in iteration 0; after the NN rolls block keys and the DataNodes drop that key, every later replaceBlock SASL handshake fails BlockTokenSecretManager.retrieveDataEncryptionKey (allKeys.get(keyId)==null) and the balancer moves no more bytes.
same_root_cause: The failing DEK comes from KeyManager.newDataEncryptionKey (server/balancer/KeyManager.java ~line 113-121 in the buggy tree), which generates encryptionKey only when it is null and never checks encryptionKey.expiryDate, so the DEK made from block key K is reused after K expired and was removed by the DataNodes' removeExpiredKeys; the DataNode then throws at BlockTokenSecretManager.java:482. This is exactly the hunk the fix changes in KeyManager.newDataEncryptionKey (`if (encryptionKey == null || encryptionKey.expiryDate < timer.now())` regenerates from the current block key); the BlockTokenSecretManager hunks only swap Time.now() for an injectable Timer.
realistic: Yes. MiniDFSCluster with dfs.encrypt.data.transfer and block access tokens on; the balancer is driven exactly as Balancer#run does (one connector, a new Balancer per iteration). The only acceleration is setKeyUpdateIntervalForTesting/setTokenLifetime(2 s) on the NN before the balancer starts, which shrinks the configurable key-roll interval and token lifetime (the same hooks upstream TestEncryptedTransfer#testLongLivedClient uses); the balancer learns these values through the normal getBlockKeys export. Key rolling, DN key removal and the failing moves are all produced by the system's own protocol; the test only waits for the DNs to drop the key. No reflection, mocks or direct calls into the check.
fixed_version: On the buggy tree plus the fix's production changes, the test passes in both runs (NOT_REPRODUCED): no InvalidEncryptionKeyException in the output, and bytes moved go from 100 before the key expiry to 400 after, versus 100 -> 100 with 9 InvalidEncryptionKeyException occurrences on the buggy tree.
reason: The agent's failing execution is driven by the exact defect HDFS-11741 fixes: the balancer's KeyManager caches its DataEncryptionKey forever without an expiry check, so once its block key expires on the DataNodes every encrypted block move fails. The trigger is realistic (only time-scaled key settings), and the consequence matches the JIRA (a long-running balancer stops moving blocks); the fixed version removes both the exception and the stall.
